unit_title: Mathematical Habits and Place Value to One Million

prompts.prompt: Explain problem-solving routines in your own words and give a correct example.
Use one of the unit representations (place-value chart with periods; base-ten reasoning in words) to show ten-times place-value relationships. Label the parts.
Carry out reading and writing multi-digit numbers accurately and show every step.
Apply comparing multi-digit numbers in a situation you have not worked before. Show the process that produced your answer.
A learner compared 4,318 and 985 and wrote 985 > 4,318, explaining that 9 is the biggest digit. Find the error, correct it, and explain why the correction works.
Explain how the ten-times relationship between neighboring places makes both comparing and rounding multi-digit numbers possible.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Build a Ten Times Bigger explainer showing place-value relationships with models, comparisons, and a rounding decision made for a stated purpose.
Name one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves your accuracy, and one question you still have.

unit_title: Multiplicative Comparison, Factors, Multiples, and Patterns

prompts.prompt: Explain multiplicative comparison statements in your own words and give a correct example.
Use one of the unit representations (comparison bar models; arrays showing factor pairs) to show equations for comparison. Label the parts.
Carry out additive versus multiplicative comparison accurately and show every step.
Apply factor pairs within 100 in a situation you have not worked before. Show the process that produced your answer.
Ann has 4 stickers and Ben has three times as many. A learner answered that Ben has 7 stickers. Find the error, correct it, and explain why the correction works.
Explain how the factor pairs of a number decide whether it is prime or composite, and how a rule-generated pattern can show a feature the rule never mentioned.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Build a Number Portrait set: for each chosen number show its factor pairs, several multiples, its prime or composite status, and a comparison story.
